title: Missing Rate Limiting
description: The API endpoint does not restrict the number of requests a user can make in a given timeframe. This allows attackers to perform brute-force attacks, credential stuffing, or cause Denial of Service (DoS).
fix: Implement rate limiting middleware (e.g., express-rate-limit). Return a 429 Too Many Requests status code when limits are exceeded.

title: API Version Bypass Risk
description: Including the API version directly in the URL (e.g., /api/v1/) can leave older, insecure versions of the API exposed if they are not explicitly decommissioned.
fix: Implement a strict deprecation policy for old API versions. Ensure security patches are applied across all active versions.
attack_paths: Exploit unpatched vulnerability in /v1/ endpoint while /v2/ is secure

title: Missing Security Headers
description: The server does not include standard HTTP security headers (like X-Content-Type-Options, Strict-Transport-Security, or X-Frame-Options), leaving the client vulnerable to MIME-sniffing, clickjacking, and man-in-the-middle attacks.
fix: Use a security middleware like Helmet in Node.js to automatically apply safe HTTP headers.

title: SQL Injection (SQLi)
description: Untrusted user input is concatenated directly into a database query. This allows an attacker to manipulate the query logic, bypassing authentication or extracting unauthorized data.
fix: Use parameterized queries, prepared statements, or a secure ORM (like Prisma or Sequelize). Never use string concatenation for SQL queries.

title: Cross-Site Scripting (XSS)
description: The application includes untrusted data in a web page without proper validation or escaping, allowing attackers to execute malicious JavaScript in the victim's browser.
fix: Contextually encode all output. Implement a strong Content Security Policy (CSP). Use modern frameworks (React, Vue) that escape output by default.
